items.title: House of the week: Home with saltwater pool in coveted Mississauga neighbourhood
items.summary: This place: Home with a saltwater pool in a coveted Mississauga neighbourhood. Features: This custom-built residence, completed in 2020, is nestled in the coveted Lorne Park community and offers over 5,100 square feet of living space. The open-concept main floor sets the tone, with hardwood flooring and LED lighting. The kitchen features white quartz countertops, built-in KitchenAid and Bosch appliances, custom cabinetry, a walk-in pantry and an exposed brick feature wall. Upstairs, four bedrooms include a primary bedroom with an ensuite bathroom and a walk-in closet. The additional bedrooms have semi-ensuite bathrooms or ensuite bathrooms and closets. The finished basement features a home cinema, a recreation space, a full bathroom and storage. The backyard boasts a heated saltwater concrete pool, professional landscaping, exterior mood lighting and a fully fenced yard. Additional highlights include hardwired internet for every TV, custom blinds throughout, a water filtration system, security cameras with doorbell consoles on every floor and a double garage. The home is just moments from schools, Whiteoaks Park, Jack Darling Memorial Park, Lake Ontario, Clarkson Village, Port Credit, boutique shopping, restaurants, golf clubs, GO Transit and the QEW.

items.title: Mississauga Reminds Residents of New Fireworks Bylaw as Diwali Celebrations Begin
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is reminding residents to follow its newer fireworks bylaw as Diwali celebrations run from Nov. 6 to 10, with the main day falling on Sunday, Nov. 8. According to the city, family and backyard fireworks can be set off without a permit on private property only on Nov. 8, while a permit is required to use them on any other day or to hold a display in a city park or other public space. Officials said fireworks are never allowed on roads, sidewalks, in parking lots or elsewhere on public property. The city said it is adding extra bylaw enforcement officers this year after receiving a record 432 complaints about Diwali fireworks during the 2025 festival. Residents were also reminded not to call 911 over fireworks unless there is immediate danger, such as a fire or injury, and to instead report illegal fireworks through the city's 311 line or website.

items.title: Jackknifed Truck Shuts Down All Express Lanes on Highway 401 in Mississauga
items.summary: All express lanes on Highway 401 in Mississauga were shut down Friday morning after a crash involving a jackknifed truck, according to the Ministry of Transportation's 511 traffic site. The Ontario Provincial Police confirmed the express lanes were closed while crews responded to the scene. Ministry of Transportation photos showed the jackknifed truck surrounded by emergency vehicles as crews worked to clear the wreckage. Police advised drivers to expect delays if travelling through the area and urged them to plan alternate routes where possible. Traffic backed up significantly in the express lanes as the cleanup continued into the morning.

items.title: Peel Police Data Shows 332 Vehicles Stolen in Mississauga Over Two Months, Clustered Near Square One and Pearson
items.summary: Peel Regional Police data shows 332 vehicles were reported stolen in Mississauga between Sept. 1 and Oct. 31, averaging more than six thefts a day across the two-month span. According to the force's online crime-mapping tool, the thefts were not evenly spread across the city, with notable clusters forming around Square One and Pearson International Airport. The interactive map, available on the Peel Regional Police website, plots the approximate location of each reported theft. Police noted that some points on the map may represent more than one vehicle stolen in the same area. The tool allows residents to see where auto thefts have been concentrated in recent months across the region.

items.title: Churchill Meadows Pool Back in Service After Sprinkler Leak Forced Months-Long Closure
items.summary: The indoor pool at Mississauga's $51-million Churchill Meadows Community Centre is back in regular use after an unexpected leak in the facility's sprinkler system forced an emergency closure at the end of summer, the city says. According to the City of Mississauga, crews have completed the repairs and reopened both the 25-metre, six-lane pool and the adjoining therapeutic pool. Drop-in swimming resumed earlier this week, and the city said regular registered programming is set to pick back up this Saturday. While the pool was shut down, aquatic programs were cancelled or shifted to other community centres nearby. The city acknowledged in its update that the closure created inconvenience for residents and added pressure on nearby facilities and staff. The community centre, which opened in late 2021 and also includes a triple gym and a teaching kitchen, sits on a 57-acre site on Ninth Line near Erin Centre Boulevard that includes Mattamy Sports Park.

items.title: Mississauga Changes Leaf Pickup Zones Ahead of This Fall's Vacuum Collection
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says its seasonal vacuum leaf pickup program is underway again this fall, though collection dates and zone boundaries have shifted for 2026. According to the city, the program is only available on streets that are more than 35 years old and lined with a significant number of large, mature trees, so not every neighbourhood qualifies. The city divides eligible areas into three colour-coded collection zones, yellow, blue and green, each with two scheduled pickup periods over the fall season. Officials are urging residents to check which zone their street falls under before raking leaves to the curb, since this year's zone map differs from previous years. The city said the program is meant to keep heavy leaf buildup off residential streets and out of storm drains as the season progresses.

items.title: City Opens Its Downtown Model to Visitors for World Urbanism Day on Nov. 8
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is marking World Urbanism Day on Nov. 8 by inviting residents to explore the tools and resources planners use to shape the city's streets, parks and public spaces. According to the city, the Mississauga Civic Centre is open to the public and houses the Downtown Model, a miniature replica of the downtown core that shows how landmarks, buildings, streets and parks fit together, including Kariya Park and Square One. The city said planners consider how people move through the city and how roads, walkways and green spaces connect as neighbourhoods evolve over time. Officials are also inviting residents to a follow-up urban design open house on Nov. 19 to meet city planning staff and learn about the ongoing review of the city's urban design program. The city said the events are meant to give residents a better sense of the decisions behind the streets, parks and trails they use every day.
